statement: Find the polynomial $P(x)$ with real coefficients such that $P(2)=12$ and $P(x^2)=x^2(x^2+1)P(x)$ for each $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

The sequence $(a_n)$ is defined by $a_1=1$ and $a_n=a_{n-1}+\dfrac{1}{n^3}$ for $n>1$.\n(a) Prove that $a_n<\dfrac{5}{4}$ for all $n$.\n(b) Given $\varepsilon>0$, find the smallest natural number $n_0$ such that $|a_{n+1}-a_n|<\varepsilon$ for all $n>n_0$.

We know that $k$ is a positive integer and the equation $x^3+y^3-2y(x^2-xy+y^2)=k^2(x-y)$ has one solution $(x_0,y_0)$ with $x_0,y_0\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$ and $x_0\neq y_0$. Prove that (i) the equation has finitely many solutions $(x,y)$ with $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$, $x\neq y$; (ii) it is possible to find 11 additional different solutions $(X,Y)$ as functions of $x_0,y_0$.

Let $OX_1,OX_2$ be rays in the interior of a convex angle $XOY$ such that $\angle XOX_1=\angle YOY_1<\dfrac{1}{3}\angle XOY$. Points $K$ on $OX_1$ and $L$ on $OY_1$ are fixed with $OK=OL$, and points $A,B$ vary on rays $OX,OY$ respectively such that the area of pentagon $OAKLB$ remains constant. Prove that the circumcircle of triangle $OAB$ passes through a fixed point other than $O$.
